articles.title: ‘What’s the safest way to defrost chicken?’ We answered your food safety questions
articles.summary: We hosted a live Q&A with guest experts Rachel Sherman and Caroline L Schauer. The Drexel food lab tested the best air fryers (the Cosori, a hands-down winner), the best nonstick cookware ( Our Place, trendy and top of the line) and much more.
body: Adrian from Toronto, Canada asks in a callout question: How do I make my fridge work better? In my mini fridge, cans sometimes get so cold that they explode, and sometimes milk goes bad faster. Is uneven refrigeration something I can improve, or is it just a sign of a bad fridge?

Rachel: My first thought here is to make sure your refrigerator is not overfilled. Uneven refrigeration could be due to lack of airflow if you have too much on your shelves. If this is not the case, it would be best to call in a professional. It could be something like a poor seal or an issue with the coils.
This is a little out of my expertise so I would definitely get someone in to take a look at it.

articles.title: Self-destructive or helpful? How to harness envy for your benefit
articles.summary: In her new book, Envy, Stacy Kim explains how to understand the feeling, identify your deeper desires and use them to achieve your goals. In the 16th-century poem The Faerie Queene, envy is a ghoulish figure riding a ravenous wolf, sad to see the fortune of others and “wonderous glad” of their…
body: Maybe not. “I think that when we don’t examine our envy, that’s when it leads us astray,” says Dr Stacy Kim, social scientist, life coach and author of the new book Envy: Why Wanting What They Have is the Key to Getting What You Want. Kim wrote the book after seeing the way envy came up for her coaching clients and reflecting on the role it had in her own life. The book is informed by social science and philosophy research, as well as her personal and professional experiences.

To Kim, a lifelong envier who says sibling rivalry propelled her to fast-track a PhD in educational policy and leadership, envy tells you “there’s something important here,” Kim says. “Envy signals to us our goals,” as well as “what is within our reach”, as we tend to envy people similar to ourselves more so than, say, superstars.
But how to transform envy from sulky to superpower? Kim gave us some points to consider.
Envy is “simply wanting something that someone else has”, Kim says. “Everyone envies – it’s normal.”

articles.title: A job that changed me: I was a rookie tour guide for art lovers – no one goes harder than active seniors in search of cultural enrichment
articles.summary: I spent time in some of the greatest art institutions with groups of self-funded retirees. But a vacation it was not. In 2012 I was living in Sydney, halfway through the shelf life of our annual theatric political satire The Wharf Revue, although I didn’t know that at the time.
body: Handling the art side of things was my gallery colleague Brian Ladd and together we landed in a wintery Manhattan in January with about 25 guests largely, shall we say, a certain demographic who were keen to sample the cultural delights of the great metropolis.

And let’s face it, there’s no shortage of them. We took in the Metropolitan Museum and the Cloisters, MoMA, the Frick, the Whitney, Radio City, the Brooklyn Museum, the Guggenheim, the High Line, half a dozen shows and several exhaustive bus tours from one end of the island to the other with our indefatigable local guide Frederique. We even managed a backstage tour of the Met, led by a volunteer who actually paid for the privilege of conducting them! A full-on schedule but, let me tell you, no one goes harder than an active senior in search of cultural enrichment. By the end of the 10 days, we were desperately in need of a holiday.

articles.title: As Peggy Flanagan Runs for Senate, a Look Back At Her Intentional Style
articles.summary: Peggy Flanagan could become the first Indigenous woman elected to the U.S. Senate. On the campaign trail, she has been using her platform to spotlight Native designers.
body: During next week’s midterm elections, Peggy Flanagan could make history as the first Indigenous woman elected to the U.S. Senate.

In the tight race to the midterms, Flanagan has been focusing on priorities such as providing affordable healthcare, maintaining climate and agricultural policies, offering better access to reproductive healthcare and abortion, and protecting the rights of local Indigenous communities. Her fashion choices on the campaign trail, however, have been just as intentional: Flanagan has been using her platform to champion Indigenous designers.

A member of the White Earth Band of Ojibwe, Flanagan has been uplifting Indigenous designs—both traditional and contemporary—on a national stage. Back at the 2024 DNC—when Flanagan was working on the Walz-Harris campaign—she wore a black and white Parfleche blazer and skirt by Jamie Okuma, one of the most prominent Indigenous designers, and the only one to be inducted into the CFDA. Flanagan accessorized the look with a pair of Copper Canoe Woman statement earrings, another contemporary Native label. “I really want those earrings,” one viewer noted, while another simply exclaimed, “She is fabulous!”

articles.title: Watch Vogue Cover Star Jenna Ortega Get Real With Her Inner Voice
articles.summary: We all have that pesky inner voice—the one that pipes up every so often, whether we want it to or not. In a new video, Vogue’s November cover star goes one-on-one with her own. And we mean that quite literally.
body: “When I prepare for a scene, I just think of every embarrassing thing that you’ve ever done, because there’s a lot,” Ortega’s inner self—whom Ortega usually tries to “keep on mute”—says, weighing in on everything from Ortega’s iconic sense of style (we don’t think Ortega ever “looks a mess,” but you presumably know best, inner voice!) to Ortega’s tendency to cry when she’s tired (relatable).

No spoilers, but by the end of the shoot, Ortega and her inner self manage to come to a kind of detente, with one of them—we won’t say who—proclaiming: “I think that this has gone pretty well.” We agree! Watch the full video for yourself above.

articles.title: How Many T-Shirts Can Be Made in a Minute?
articles.summary: Fashion is racing to automate sewing and shorten supply chain lead times. The sustainability pay-off hinges on how the industry uses the time it gains back.
body: How long does it take to make a T-shirt? The answer depends on which clock you start.

At the sewing line, a conventional cotton T-shirt requires eight person-minutes of direct labor across its sewing operations, according to Michael Hofmannrichter, co-founder and CEO of textile robotics startup Silana. This figure captures the total human input across a production line, depending on the number of people involved.

While fashion has spent decades trying to shave seconds off sewing time, this occupies only a fraction of a much longer timeline for getting a shirt to the shop floor. Designing a garment, sourcing the fabric, approving samples, placing an order and moving it to market can unfold over six to nine months. And now, the industry has another race to contend with: how long it takes to get a garment back on shelves after it’s been returned.
points: Fashion is racing to automate sewing and shorten supply chain lead times.

articles.title: The Fitbit Edge Is Everything the Charge 6 Should Have Been
articles.summary: The Fitbit Edge has good heart rate and GPS accuracy, and fixes a lot of the design flaws that frustrated me in its predecessor, the Fitbit Charge 6.
body: I’ve been using the new Fitbit Edge for a little over a week, and am happy to report that it’s quite good at its job. It shipped with more features than I expected (Google Maps directions were there from the jump) and corrects the missteps that Google made with the Fitbit Charge 6. After running the Fitbit Edge through its paces, here’s my breakdown of what works well, what doesn’t, and what I think of the device overall.

When I reviewed it in May 2025, I liked a lot about the Charge 6, but found it had a few serious flaws. Tightening the strap messed up its GPS readings (weird but true), and some of its features required a subscription (like the music controls that only worked with YouTube Music). Its promised side button wasn’t really a button, and didn’t even always work.
I’m happy to report that all of my biggest gripes have been fixed in the Fitbit Edge. Or to put it another way: the Edge is what the Charge should have been in the first place.
points: The Fitbit Edge has good heart rate and GPS accuracy, and fixes a lot of the design flaws that frustrated me in its predecessor, the Fitbit Charge 6.

articles.title: Can Halloween Be Chic? 6 Tastemakers on How to Throw a Kitsch-Free Spooky Season Party
articles.summary: Zoë de Givenchy, Romilly Newman, Rebecca Gardner, and Kelly Wearstler share tips on how to host a chic Halloween event.
body: It’s been my job to party. After years covering frivolities and fêtes as Vogue Parties editor, the following may come as a surprise: I loathe Halloween and everything about it. I dislike having to dress up in costume, I dislike being spooked, and I dislike the color combination of black and orange. There’s little about the holiday that appeals.

Part of what drew me to the world of parties was the glamour of it all. Events filled with floral arrangements rivaling a Jan van Huysum botanical tableau. Gorgeously pressed linens with more starch than a bucket of French fries. A room full of bodies dressed in black tie and clutching decorous minaudières. It’s just not right to carry a bag jumbled with life’s necessities; upon entering a fabulous party, those quotidian realities should be left at the door! And when it comes to Halloween parties, specifically, what’s also left at the door? Anything resembling chic.
De Givenchy: Yes, if you keep it dark and sexy and glamorous. Think low lighting, your best silver, and killer cocktails.
points: Zoë de Givenchy, Romilly Newman, Rebecca Gardner, and Kelly Wearstler share tips on how to host a chic Halloween event.
